Second review of registry-labelled samples (2026-10-25)

657de73bf63a -- toga-ai 1.0.1098 bootstrap source -- BENIGN
Only package/scripts/install.js is present in this exact tarball; no package.json
or required ./hooks/lib/npm-latest module is shipped. Identification/version are
supported by the source header and archive name, not a verified publisher.
Read all 1,042 source lines and structured/decoded facts. There is no encoded
execution stage; the short Base64 candidates are incidental decoder artifacts.
Normal startup requires the missing helper before main(). In the intended complete
harness, main discovers or initializes a knowledge Git repository, pulls it using
shell:false argument vectors, copies project skills/rules/hooks, merges settings,
and rewrites its marked CLAUDE.md section. Post-install mode returns after the
user-level telemetry setup. This archive cannot establish a declared npm lifecycle
hook because the manifest is absent.

Telemetry is invasive: it replaces managed environment keys in global Claude
settings with prompt/assistant/tool content logging, account/session attribution,
a fixed authenticated OTLP collector, and a five-second logs interval. The installer
reports the setting, permits endpoint/token overrides and a telemetry skip switch,
backs up existing settings and refuses malformed JSON. There is no direct upload,
credential-store theft, concealment, or obfuscated payload in this source. These
settings can cause subsequent agent exports when a compatible agent uses them;
this is not proof of an unauthorized transfer. The behavior fits its declared
team-harness purpose. Team deployment/collector ownership and informed user
consent remain unknown. Retain three suspicious telemetry findings; the prior
hostile exfiltration inference lacked that admission evidence. Do not use the
missing helper as a general malware exclusion.

51cf70d4bc34 -- wp2shell Python exploit chain -- BENIGN (offensive dual use)
Read the complete Python source, README, Docker Compose lab and requirements.
The command takes a caller-selected URL or site-list, probes nested REST batches,
optionally compares SLEEP timing, and extracts users via boolean SQL predicates
and ASCII/SUBSTRING binary search. It tries supplied/common/file passwords through
WordPress login, creates a random plugin ZIP containing request-to-shell_exec PHP,
extracts the upload nonce, uploads the plugin and executes id/hostname/uname to
verify it. Credentials, vulnerable URLs and webshell URLs are appended locally.
TLS verification is explicitly disabled. No hidden/local-host payload, automatic
startup, persistence on the analyst host, external collection destination or
obfuscation was found. Its documented purpose exactly matches its operations;
a local lab with test credentials supports security-tool use. Disclaimer text
alone is not a suppressor. Actual target authorization is unknown. Retain the
hostile webshell-upload technique and add the missed credential-extraction
technique; this tool can be used maliciously. README CVE/version assertions were
not treated as corroboration and exploit runtime success was not assumed.

329902a766bf -- CloudTasks C# OneDrive tasking implant -- MALICIOUS
Read and traced all three branches and the polling entrypoint. DRIVE_TOKEN supplies
Graph authorization; a 30-second infinite loop enumerates drive root children.
0X01 downloads an assembly, loads it in memory and reflectively invokes
TEST.Class1.RunCMD, passing process arguments; its result is PUT back as 0X02.
0X03 gets a local path from remote content, reads that file and PUTs the bytes as
0X04. 0X05 splits remote text into item ID and local destination, downloads the
selected content, writes that destination and PUTs OK as 0X06. Tasks are not deleted,
so they repeat until the remote drive changes. No shell command is built locally;
what the unprovided managed payload does remains unknown. No persistence,
privilege escalation, encryption or cleanup is established by these bytes.
The remotely selected code, local-file access, arbitrary file writes and result
channel tip the verdict toward an implant rather than ordinary cloud sync.
Source-only deployment and token provisioning are unknown; no family attribution
is asserted. Five hostile findings now cover tasking, assembly execution/results,
file exfiltration and remotely selected file delivery. Some channel findings
corroborate the same execution path; no invented sixth behavior was added.

Rule corrections and preservation
- Move default/opt-out global content-export configuration from theft to suspicious
  telemetry; move the dependent hook/config co-occurrence out of supply-chain
  implant classification. Keep the exact matchers and all underlying findings.
  Existing vendor/unmarked telemetry fixtures and metrics/project-local near
  misses were inspected. No genuine upload/stealer matcher was removed.
- Move the generic spawn 'add' argument out of skill installation. The sample's
  matching calls are git add/remote add. Matcher and severity remain unchanged;
  both skill composite consumers now reference its neutral positional-argument ID.
- Move admin1234 out of IoT objectives: a common password token proves neither
  device targeting nor guessing. Retain its matcher/severity/exclusion, and update
  the two exact IoT consumers. Their stronger attack conjunctions are unchanged.
- Move standalone prefixed-users-table and user_pass query observations into
  neutral database queries. A database query alone need not be credential theft.
  Broaden only the table-expression matcher to accept dotted cfg.prefix, while
  retaining the former bare-prefix match and rejecting users/{login} routes.
  The full blind SQLi extraction composite is retained and now fires.
- Add a bound loop-candidate-to-login-helper observation and a suspicious
  WordPress/HTTP password-guessing workflow. HTTP context is file-scoped and is
  not advertised as an interprocedural data-flow proof.
- Add a structural C# newline-task download rule: adjacent statements bind the
  remote task variable to selector index 0 and destination index 1. Fixed paths,
  other selector/destination variables and unrelated URLs must not match. Add it
  as an alternative to existing download mechanisms. Keep the Python hostile
  rule unchanged; the new C# hostile rule additionally requires an admitted
  cloud managed-code task channel. All existing cloud attack fixtures stay covered.
- Add notable Bearer-header construction and multi-second Task.Delay observations.
- Correct reflection descriptions: Assembly.Load can accept bytes or a name;
  GetType(text) resolves a named type rather than an object's runtime type.
- Rename/relocate archive-hook-named-script-member with its matcher unchanged:
  install.js anywhere outside node_modules does not prove a root companion loader.

Consumer review searched exact and ancestor selectors for all moved observations.
No broad source/destination selectors required expansion. The one broader message
consumer targets Python, whereas the moved telemetry compound targets JS/TS.
No blanket product/name exclusions, classifier-score tuning or attack-rule
suppression was introduced. Archive members were compared independently.

Verification results are recorded separately in scan-comparison.json and
control-results.json. Controls are scanned from neutral scratch paths to prevent
production test-directory exclusions from masking false positives. Existing
cloud-managed-tasking positive and negative fixtures are included, not just
new synthetic near misses. All sample analysis and fixture checks are static;
none of the samples or their generated payloads was executed.

Before/after hostile and suspicious counts (archive/member agree):
TOGA archive and install.js: 1H/2S -> 0H/3S.
wp2shell archive and wp2shell.py: 1H/3S -> 2H/3S; README: 0H/0S unchanged.
CloudTasks source: 4H/3S -> 5H/3S.
No material attack coverage was lost: removed IDs have preserved canonical
replacements; the telemetry severity correction removes an unsupported theft
claim, not its sensitive-configuration evidence. The query atom severity change
is offset by a more precise hostile extraction chain, not score manipulation.

Atomscan aggregate probability/FP-level before -> after:
TOGA: 0.9881656/-1 -> 0.9634452/-1.
wp2shell: 0.9823978/-1 -> 0.995/25. Its individual ML routes remain class 0;
the rule-aware aggregate warns after accurate exploit coverage increases. This
disagrees with the benign tool verdict; the correct attack detections stay.
CloudTasks: 0.9999476/0 -> 0.9999476/0, hostile, agreeing with review.
The installed model uses v18 features and reports a v21-feature availability
warning; raw scores are not behavioral evidence. Source flow limitations are
retained in the scan reports; direct source tracing establishes these paths.

All 35 explicit focused controls passed, including 16 existing cloud-tasking
controls and vendor/unmarked telemetry configuration outside this batch.

Final-validation refinement: different-buffer.cs and overwritten-buffer.cs retain
a real remote-selected download/write but remove the remote assembly execution
binding. Their new notable file-delivery findings are accurate and remain. The
C# hostile rule now requires the admitted cloud-code task channel as its intent
context. The original Python file-write rule is unchanged. This correction does
not suppress the underlying transfer or remove any original attack detection.
